name: Delhi

topAttractions.name: Qutub Minar
topAttractions.description: The tallest minaret in India, built in 1199 by Qutb-ud-din Aibak, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a symbol of Delhi's rich history.

topAttractions.name: Red Fort
topAttractions.description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site, the Red Fort was built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in 1648 and served as the imperial palace for nearly 200 years.

topAttractions.name: India Gate
topAttractions.description: A war memorial built in 1931, India Gate is a 42-meter tall structure that honors the soldiers who died in World War I and the Third Anglo-Afghan War.

bestTimeToVisit: October to March, when the weather is mild and pleasant, making it ideal for sightseeing and outdoor activities.
culturalFact: Delhi is home to the ancient Indraprastha, the capital of the Pandavas in the Hindu epic, the Mahabharata.

hiddenGem.name: Hauz Khas Village
hiddenGem.description: A charming village in South Delhi, known for its ancient architecture, boutique shops, and vibrant nightlife.

relatedFestival: Diwali, the Festival of Lights, is celebrated with great fervor in Delhi, with the city's streets and homes illuminated with diyas and lights.
passportTieIn: If you have stamps or wishlist items for the Red Fort, Qutub Minar, or India Gate, they will appear here! These iconic landmarks are a must-visit for any traveler to Delhi.
